limitations: Unrelated AiDotNet.Tensors parity testhost began running during measurement. Timings are exploratory, not a controlled speedup versus the earlier run.
Warm GPU calls reuse internal scratch/device storage; every call still owns fresh outputs/history and includes validation, upload, kernel execution and readback.
TA-Lib native owns output arrays but does not preserve bar history or publish presence flags.
Periodic binary grid inputs favor exact SMA certification. Arbitrary uncertified SMA data is unsupported in required GPU mode.
Only this AMD OpenCL device/driver was tested. No automatic crossover or global rollout is enabled.
first_call_note: Setup calls and initialization durations are retained in the compressed log. Process and driver caches can already be warm.
changes: Bounded internal host scratch/device buffer reuse, never pooling public results/history.
Direct Asin flags derived during validation; composed flags proven from domain bounds when possible; otherwise read from device.
Uninitialized output arrays, fully written before publication.
Large fused histories use one owned contiguous array while retaining chunk views for existing consumers.
